newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy set to expel scores of illegal immigrants.
newsitem.headline: Italy set to expel scores of illegal immigrants.

text.p: Italian police prepared on Thursday to send nearly 80 would-be illegal immigrants detained over the New Year holiday back to North Africa.

Police said the clandestine travellers, who were intercepted in two operations on the island of Lampedusa and in surrounding waters, would be taken to the town of Agrigento in southern Sicily and served with expulsion orders.
Police intercepted 39 Moroccans before dawn on Wednesday in Lampedusa and 40 other North Africans just before midnight on Tuesday in nearby waters.
The latter group had set out from Tunisia eight days earlier and told police that four of their companions had died of cold on the voyage and had been thrown overboard.

Police said on Thursday, however, that the immigrants had been lying. "It was a bluff to reach the Sicilian coast and avoid being sent back immediately to North Africa," said a spokesman for the finance police, which picked up the motorboat.
Prosecutors in Agrigento said they had opened an inquiry into the incident.
The island of Lampedusa, midway between North Africa and Sicily, is a favoured "back-door" entry point to Italy.
Illegal immigrants who are caught are moved to Sicily and served with expulsion orders but most then head north to mainland Italy and other European countries, police say.
